concerns.message: Acceptance item 3 still says "a target emptied by collection or theft goes stale". After the attempt-1 fix, a journal rumor can only point at an island (a sealed source) or a cache sector. Theft moves a rubbing from one player to another and can never empty a sealed source or a cache. Only a carrier target can be emptied by theft, and carrier sightings are now one-shot and never go stale. The 'theft' half of this item is a leftover from the rejected design and can't be satisfied as written.
concerns.consequence: The worker has two options. It can bring back carrier-rumor staleness to write a 'theft makes it stale' test, which is exactly the tracker leak decisions.md removed and which item 5 ('no stale message is ever sent for a carrier sighting') forbids. Or it can hit the Stop rule on contradicting acceptance and report blocked/question mid-run. Change the item to 'emptied by collection (a source collected, a cache claimed)'. If the intent was the holder obtaining the type by theft, say 'a rumor whose type the holder then steals is resolved, not stale'.

concerns.message: The targeted rumor is gold-gated by the caller, but `stepIntel` only returns `{ state, messages }`. It gives no per-request outcome and no request id. Several cases are valid under this design yet produce no rumor: the 30-s carrier-sighting cap, no eligible target (only the requester's own inventory is left, or every copy is carried and has no 30-s-old sample yet), the type already held, or an unknown or departed player. §11 also requires purchases to carry an idempotent request id so retries can't double-spend.
concerns.consequence: objectives-endgame can't tell whether to charge 25 gold. Either players pay for nothing when the cap or an empty pool blocks the rumor, or the caller has to parse message kinds to decide billing. A retried request generates a second rumor, consumes rng and can burn the sighting cap. Fixing this later changes the public step shape this feature is meant to freeze. Before workers start, settle a request `{ requestId, playerId, type }` and a returned `outcomes: { requestId, result: 'rumor' | 'sighting' | 'capped' | 'none' | 'duplicate' }` (or an exported pure `targetedRumorAvailability` query), with repeated request ids answered without mutating state.

concerns.message: Losses and completions come from diffing 'each player's held types'. The plan doesn't say whether rubbings reserved in a duel count as held. The ledger's `heldTypes` counts them (objectives/state.ts:274-285), but a caller that builds the view from `location.kind === 'player'` would drop them. The plan also doesn't say what happens when a player leaves and their rubbings go to a cache.
concerns.consequence: If reserved rubbings aren't counted, every duel start looks like a loss of all types. Players would get spurious fresh rumors (and possibly carrier sightings that use up their cap), full-set routes would go inactive, and a draw or cancel would look like a new completion and send the route again. A departed player would be sent a fresh rumor. State in the view type and in docs/intel.md that held types include duel-reserved rubbings and that left players are excluded, and add a scripted test for duel start → draw that expects no messages.

concerns.message: The one-per-30-s sighting cap also blocks the two free triggers: the §11 fresh rumor after a loss and the journal replacement. The plan doesn't say what the player gets instead: nothing, a deferred sighting, or a 'no lead yet' message. A sighting also needs a sample at least 30 s old, which doesn't exist in the first 30 s after control start.
concerns.consequence: A player who loses two types within 30 s silently gets no free rumor, which breaks §11's 'give them a free fresh rumor'. Different workers or tests will each pick their own behaviour, and the EXERCISED check can't cover a kind nobody defined. Name the outcome (for example a `no-lead` message to the player, or a pending lead delivered when the cap lifts) and test it.

concerns.message: The carrier history keeps only a sector per copy. A copy just stolen from the requester was, 30 s earlier, in the requester's own hands or reserved in their duel. The rule 'never a target that is the player's own inventory' can't be checked against a sample that doesn't record who held it.
concerns.consequence: A victim's free fresh rumor can be a sighting of the sector where they themselves stood 30 s ago. It is useless to them and wastes the one sighting they get per 30 s. Record the owner kind and player in each internal sample (ids never leave the state) and exclude samples held by the requester.

concerns.message: If the history is stored literally as per-copy samples over the last 30 s, that is 600 ticks × 8–12 copies = 4,800–7,200 entries. Each tick copies them immutably, and the replay hashes all of it, over a 36,000-tick seed plus replays.
concerns.consequence: The long property seed is slow enough to hit vitest's 5 s default, or it forces a long custom timeout. Per-tick hashing, if a worker adds it, would take minutes. Store only sector changes per copy (tick, sector, holder), pruned to the newest entry at or before now − delay. This gives the same answer, including across skipped ticks, and the state stays tiny.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: Replace the per-copy rolling 30-s history with one carrier-sector snapshot taken at each 30-s carrier boundary counted from control start. Keep the latest two snapshots (sector, type and internal holder per carried copy). A carrier sighting returns an entry from the older snapshot, so it is always 30–60 s old. The minute-28 broadcast reads the newer one. The per-player cap then lines up with the same boundaries: at most one sighting per player per snapshot. One mechanism serves both the sightings and the minute-28 reveal. The state is bounded by two small arrays, skipped ticks are handled by the same boundary-crossing rule the reveals already use, and 'never the current location' holds by construction. The cost is a sighting age of 30–60 s instead of exactly 30 s. That still fits §11's 'coarse, delayed' wording, though it would be a deliberate relaxation of decisions.md's 'always the sector from 30 s earlier'.

It steps a naive immutable state of 8 players and 12 rubbings through 36,000 ticks, appends a per-copy (tick, sector) sample every tick with 600-tick pruning, and hashes the final state twice for the replay check. Time it against a version that stores sector changes only (and against the two-snapshot variant). If the naive version takes more than about 2 s or needs a raised timeout, adopt change-only or snapshot storage in the plan now.
